theme.rationale: A professional quant-finance terminal demands a dark, high-contrast environment to reduce eye strain during prolonged data analysis. The aesthetic is 'Bloomberg terminal meets modern SaaS', heavily utilizing 'Grid Borders' and 'Retro-Futurism' micro-themes (specifically terminal-like data density without the cyberpunk kitsch).

font_families.monospace: JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, monospace

rules.headings: Use tight tracking (tracking-tight) for all headings. Never use Inter or generic sans for headings.
rules.numbers: ALL financial data, ticker symbols, prices, equations, and tabular data MUST use JetBrains Mono to ensure tabular lining and vertical alignment of decimals.
rules.labels: Overlines and table headers should be uppercase, text-[10px] to text-xs, tracking-widest, text-zinc-400.

rules: Use tight gaps (gap-4 or gap-px with border-collapse) for data correlations and scanability.
Eliminate unnecessary padding. Use p-4 for standard widgets, p-2 for dense lists.
Use grid layout extensively. Expose the skeleton using the 'Grid Borders' surface strategy (1px border-border/40 on grid items).
Dashboards should consume the full width (max-w-full or max-w-[1920px]). No standard narrow containers.
Grid items must be direct children of the grid container to prevent subgrid breaking.
layout_and_spacing.surface_strategy: Grid Borders (Technical Look). Expose the grid layout with 1px hard borders and no shadows. Flat solid backgrounds. Sharp edges (rounded-none or maximum rounded-sm). No glassmorphism on the main data panels to avoid visual refraction of critical numbers.

tables.style: Highly dense. Use JetBrains Mono for all cell data. Right-align all numeric columns. Use conditional text colors (signals.buy_positive/sell_negative) for returns and signals. Sticky header.
tables.shadcn_customization: Override default Shadcn Table padding to be tighter (py-2 px-3). Remove rounded corners.

cards.style: Cardless or Technical Borders. 1px solid border (#27272A), completely flat background (#121212), zero shadow, sharp corners (rounded-none or rounded-sm).

buttons.style: Tactile and functional. Primary buttons use the accent blue (#2563EB). Signal action buttons (Buy/Sell) must use solid green/red. Sharp corners. Use specific transition styles for hover states.

libraries: d3 (for complex Monte Carlo fan charts)
charts.style: Dark background (#050505), hide standard grid lines or make them extremely subtle (stroke: #27272A, strokeDasharray: '3 3'). Data lines must be neon/high-contrast with a subtle drop-shadow (blur-sm) to simulate a glowing terminal effect.
charts.monte_carlo: For Monte Carlo fan charts, use stacked Recharts Area elements with decreasing opacities (e.g., fill: #3B82F6, fillOpacity: 0.1 to 0.4) to represent confidence intervals.

navigation.style: Left sidebar or highly compact top-bar. Solid background (#050505) with 1px border. Links should be subtle, turning pure white on active state.

rules: Minimalist and snappy. No bouncy animations.
Use micro-interactions for feedback (e.g., hover states on table rows with extremely fast transitions: transition-colors duration-75).
Chart rendering should have a fast entrance animation (e.g., Recharts default ease-in).

icons.style: Stroke width 1.5. Keep sizes small (14px to 16px) to match the dense data aesthetic.

images.usage: Use as a dark, lowered-opacity background image for the login/auth screen or a landing/welcome page. Overlay with bg-black/80.

accessibility.contrast: Maintain WCAG AA (4.5:1) minimum. Dark theme text uses pure white (#FFFFFF) against #121212 surface for maximum clarity.
accessibility.focus: All interactive elements must have focus:ring-1 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:outline-none.
accessibility.testing: All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute (e.g., data-testid='buy-signal-button', data-testid='stock-price-display').

UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. Avoid the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Create a distinctive, high-end professional quant terminal.
All implementations MUST use standard React .js files, NOT .tsx files. Follow vanilla JS semantics and PropTypes where necessary.
DO NOT use Inter or standard sans-serifs for headings. You must use Chivo or IBM Plex Sans for headings, and JetBrains Mono for all numeric/tabular data.
DO NOT use generic centered layouts. Use highly dense, data-driven grids. Align numbers right, text left.
DO NOT use gradients for surfaces. Use flat, dark colors with 1px crisp borders.
Never use AI assistant emoji characters for icons. Use Lucide icons.
DO NOT use complete transparent backgrounds for the header, sidebar, or dropdowns. They must have a solid dark background (#050505 or #121212).
All data metrics MUST use the monospace font to ensure decimal points align vertically. Use consistent decimal places (e.g., 2 decimal places for prices).
Apply precise text colors (Green/Red) to positive/negative values and signals to build immediate visual correlations.
Implement the AI quant analyst summary using formatted monospace blocks for mathematical equations to maintain the terminal aesthetic.
